clue.text: Daily one draws from benevolent societies

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaning lady, also called a char
one is the Roman numeral I
draws are tied games, ties

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman picks charities to give to from a list of good causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb but is the British noun for a cleaner who comes in each day, a char.
explanation.definitionFit: Charities are organisations set up to do good, which is what benevolent societies are.

clue.text: Rumours about the use of two faculties

parts.note: hearing is one of the senses, so hear
speech is the other faculty, so say

explanation.surface: Gossip arises from using both your ears and your mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Two faculties, hearing and speaking, give the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is information passed on by word of mouth, unverified gossip.

clue.text: He danced with a girl, this Elizabethan knight

indicators.note: danced signals the letters of he and a girl moving about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A courtier at Queen Elizabeth's court dances with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'danced' rearranges HE and A GIRL. Sir Walter Raleigh was a favourite of Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an explorer and courtier knighted under Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Processions the queen held in these grounds

indicators.note: held in says the queen's letters sit inside the word for processions

parts.note: trains are processions or lines of followers
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Royal processions are held on these estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' is the container signal; ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword queen, and trains here are ceremonial processions, not railway ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land or ground of a particular kind; the plural matches grounds.

clue.text: Trip which was as fair as could be

indicators.note: as could be signals the letters of as fair being whatever arrangement they might form

explanation.surface: A holiday that was as pleasant as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as could be' rearranges AS FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition, especially to watch wild animals in Africa.

clue.text: Take back espresso, it was stirred with a pole!

indicators.note: stirred, as a coffee is, tells us the letters of espresso are mixed

parts.note: S is the south pole

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves their coffee after it was stirred with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' rearranges ESPRESSO into REPOSSES, then S for a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess is to reclaim goods, as a lender does when payments stop.

clue.text: Sticking to the data that's loud and real

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical term for loud
actual means real

explanation.surface: A report keeps to evidence that is clear and genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual describes what is based on facts, keeping to the information.

clue.text: Someone who needed looking after found hanging

explanation.surface: Someone in care was discovered suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependent relies on others for support; the adjective in older use also means suspended or pendent.

clue.text: A little road-rage is the norm

parts.note: Ave is the short form of avenue, a road written small
taken as written

explanation.surface: A touch of anger behind the wheel is what most drivers show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' seems to mean 'a small amount of' road rage, but 'little road' is the shortened word AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An average is the typical or standard level, what is usual.

clue.text: I'm in one river, then another, but without success

indicators.note: the letter from I'm goes inside the first river named

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
I'm reads as I am: the letter I is placed
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A swimmer moves from one river to the next and gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal (Cornwall) and Ure (Yorkshire) are English rivers that crop up often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure is a lack of success; the phrase describes the state the noun names.

clue.text: Preacher who lost the point after one page

annotationWithheld.why: Preacher who lost the point after one page (7): A (one) + P (page) leaves OSTLE, which only comes from LOST plus E (point) rearranged, so 'lost' would be both the anagram fodder and its own indicator.
annotationWithheld.clue: Preacher who lost the point after one page

clue.text: He may guess at bad times on a mountain

indicators.note: bad signals that the word times is spoilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A climber reckons wrongly how long a mountain ascent will take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' is the anagram signal; a tor is a rocky hilltop typical of Dartmoor in south-west England, and 'at' and 'on' are mere links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who estimates makes a reasoned guess at an amount or value.

clue.text: Peculiar sense of timing

explanation.surface: An odd feeling for rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or strange; in music the offbeat is an unaccented beat in the bar.

clue.text: Initial help with treatment of the sick

parts.note: initial means first
help means aid

explanation.surface: The first care given to someone who falls ill.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate care given to the injured or ill.

clue.text: Some snappy thong can be a crusher:

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tight, snappy piece of underwear can squeeze painfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A python kills its prey by constriction, squeezing it to death.

clue.text: A distant hope for a Meershaum, perhaps

explanation.surface: A tobacco pipe's longing for something far off.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is an unrealistic fantasy; a meerschaum is a kind of tobacco pipe, so its dream would be a pipe's.

clue.text: Lotions sprinkled on it and people, way back

indicators.note: sprinkled suggests the letters are scattered about into a new order

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for way is turned round

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Creams are dabbed on a person on their way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprinkled' rearranges ON IT and MEN into OINTMEN; 'back' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ointments are smooth oily preparations rubbed into the skin, like lotions.

clue.text: Cry in a torn sari, creating pressure lines

indicators.note: the cry is put inside the jumbled garment
torn says the letters of sari are ripped apart and rearranged

parts.note: to cry is to sob

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over a ripped sari, causing a stressful scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal; 'pressure' tempts a reading about stress, but it belongs to the weather-map definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobars are lines on a weather map joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Rum men at work produce rough scrapings

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters of rum men at are busy forming a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Sailors with their rum at work produce coarse shavings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges RUM MEN AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramentum is a botanical term for thin chaffy scales or shavings.

clue.text: Cold white covers take up space on Channel Island

indicators.note: in a down clue, take up means read upwards, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: CI stands for Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy

explanation.surface: Snowy hats take up room on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take up' reverses SPACE followed by CI to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice caps are permanent sheets of ice covering polar or mountain areas.

clue.text: Insist that a lock of hair be tied back

indicators.note: back says the lock of hair is turned round, as hair tied back is pulled the other way

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone demands that a strand of hair be pulled back and fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tied back' is the reversal signal, read as the hair pulled the other way; 'that' is a link after the definition 'Insist'.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state something forcefully, to maintain it firmly.

clue.text: Sprung loose

explanation.surface: Released from prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprung means released from jail; to loose is to release, so both are freed.

clue.text: Revives and picks up again

explanation.surface: Restarts something.
explanation.definitionFit: To reopen is to start again after a break, as a case or shop resumes.

clue.text: Dispense tea in Crete-and so forth

indicators.note: dispense suggests the letters of tea and Crete are handed out in a new order

explanation.surface: Serve tea on a Greek island, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispense' scatters the letters of TEA and CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for 'and the rest', used to mean and other similar things.

clue.text: More likely she'll be there after sailor returns

indicators.note: after places the woman's pronoun behind the sailor
returns says the sailor word comes back to front

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
she in the object case is her

explanation.surface: A woman will probably be waiting once the seaman comes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns TAR into RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather means preferably or sooner, as in 'I'd rather', more readily.

clue.text: Take note; at ten turn it on

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: turn tells us to twist the letters of it on into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch the radio or television on at ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the anagram signal, disguised as switching a set on; the definition 'Take note' is the sense of the word called out as a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Attention is said as a command meaning listen carefully or pay heed.

clue.text: Wealthiest one honoured in those who remain

indicators.note: the honour letters go inside the word for those left

parts.note: the rest means the others who remain
one is the Roman numeral I
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award for those honoured

explanation.surface: The richest of a group is the one who received an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, a Companion of Honour, is a British order of merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Richest is the superlative of rich, meaning having the most money.

clue.text: Tales are told about divisions of buildings

indicators.note: are told means spoken, so the levels of a building are heard and not seen

parts.note: storeys are the floors or levels of a building

explanation.surface: Accounts are given about the floors of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: In British spelling the floors of a building are STOREYS, said just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are narratives, accounts of events real or invented.

clue.text: One who doesn't have a leg to stand on

definitions.text: One who doesn't have a leg to stand on

parts.words: One who doesn't have a leg to stand on
parts.note: the idiom for someone with a weak argument, read literally as someone missing a limb

explanation.surface: Someone whose case has no support.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has had a limb cut off may literally lack a leg.

clue.text: Put in liquid again and simmer in beer with no head

indicators.note: in beer, meaning drunk, signals that the letters of simmer reel into a new order
with no head drops the first letter of beer

explanation.surface: Dunk something in liquid again and let it bubble in ale without froth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' (as in 'in beer', tipsy) is the weak signal to mix SIMMER with EER, the beer after 'with no head' takes its B.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimmerse is to dip or plunge into a fluid a second time.
